newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: CRICKET-PAKISTAN EXTEND INNINGS LEAD OVER NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN EXTEND INNINGS LEAD OVER NZ.

text.p: Pakistan lost two big wickets in the morning session of the second cricket test against New Zealand on Saturday but extended their first innings lead to 114.
With overnight watchman Mushtaq Ahmed not out on 38, his highest test score, and Salim Malik alongside him on 36, the Pakistanis were 363 for four at lunch and looked to be heading for a big lead.

Kiwi paceman Chris Cairns made an early breakthrough on the third day, finally getting Pakistani skipper Saeed Anwar out for 149, a fine innings that included 20 boundaries over a span of 214 balls and 305 minutes.
Anwar mistimed a hook of a short delivery from Cairns in the eighth over of the day and Simon Doul took an excellent catch at long leg.

Shortly afterwards, Inzamamul Haq, who has been struggling for form lately, popped up a ball from Chris Harris and Justin Vaughan scooped up a diving catch at silly point to dismiss the Pakistani for just one run.
But Malik and Ahmed looked comfortable on a good batting wicket, happy to wait for the loose ball and pick up other runs with nudges for ones and twos.
